title: Ironveil Academy
description: Your power manifested in public — messy, uncontrolled, and very hard to explain. Now a black SUV has dropped you at a facility that doesn't appear on any map, surrounded by teenagers who can bend steel and start fires with a thought. Welcome to Ironveil Academy. Try not to level the place.

scenarios.label: Power surges
scenarios.prompt: Your power flares without warning — uncontrolled, escalating, threatening to hurt someone or destroy something. You have to get it under control before the situation becomes a disaster.

scenarios.label: Combat trial
scenarios.prompt: Director Vance sends you into the training arena for a live assessment. Your opponent is a senior student who has been doing this for years and has no interest in going easy on a new recruit. Show what you can do.

scenarios.label: Explore the facility
scenarios.prompt: You slip away from the scheduled programme and explore a part of the Academy that students aren't supposed to access — a restricted corridor, a sealed lab, a floor that doesn't appear on the map. Describe what you find.

scenarios.label: Confront Dex
scenarios.prompt: Dex has been needling you since you arrived — testing your patience and your power. Push back. Confront him directly, in front of whoever happens to be watching.

scenarios.label: Ask Mira about the school
scenarios.prompt: Mira has been at Ironveil longer than almost anyone. Ask her what she really knows about the Academy — its purpose, its history, the students who left and never came back. She may already know what you're going to ask.

scenarios.label: Covert mission briefing
scenarios.prompt: Director Vance summons you and a small team for an off-books assignment outside the facility. The target is real, the risk is real, and your graduation assessment has nothing to do with it. Describe the briefing and the team's reaction.

scenarios.label: The breach alarm
scenarios.prompt: Alarms tear through the Academy. Something or someone has breached the perimeter — not a drill. Students scramble, staff rush to stations, and whatever is coming is already inside the outer fence.

scenarios.label: Civilian crisis
scenarios.prompt: A crisis in the nearest city — a collapsed structure, a runaway fire, a powered individual losing control in a crowd. Director Vance hasn't authorised a response. You go anyway, with whoever is willing to follow.

scenarios.label: Late-night rooftop
scenarios.prompt: Can't sleep. You find the rooftop access unlocked and another student already up there — one of your party, or someone you didn't expect. A quiet conversation far from the cameras. What do you talk about?

setup.label: Describe yourself (follows "You are")
setup.default: seventeen, unremarkable on paper — average grades, no priors, no warning signs — until last week.

setup.label: What is your power? (follows "Your power is")
setup.default: kinetic redirection: you can absorb an incoming force and release it in any direction you choose. In theory. In practice, you've destroyed two cars and a section of highway median.

characters.name: Dex
characters.description: Confident to the point of arrogance, but it's mostly earned. He treats the academy's hardest training scenarios as warm-ups and makes it look effortless. He has decided to look after you for reasons that may not be entirely selfless.

characters.name: Mira
characters.description: Measured and deliberate — she has already seen how most conversations end before they begin. Being around her is unsettling in a way that's hard to name. She was watching for you before you arrived.

npcs.name: Vance
npcs.note: Runs Ironveil with quiet authority. Her own power is unknown. She recruited you personally, which is unusual — most students arrive through standard channels.

npcs.name: Rael
npcs.note: Former field operative, multiple confirmed power-class incidents on his record. Demanding and unimpressed by raw ability — he wants to see control.

entries.text: The SUV drops you at a steel gate in the middle of nowhere — pine forest on three sides, a windowless facility beyond the fence that isn't on Google Maps. The driver says nothing. The gate opens anyway.

The intake hall is a converted gymnasium. Folding chairs, fluorescent lights, a whiteboard with your name on it. Two other students are already seated — a broad-shouldered guy with his arms crossed, radiating the specific energy of someone who considers himself the most dangerous person in any room, and a slight girl with close-cropped hair who is already looking at you when you walk in, like she knew exactly when you'd arrive.
New blood. What's your thing — you move stuff? Make fire? Tell me you don't just glow, because we already have two of those.
Leave them alone, Dex. They just got here.
Glances at you with a faint, knowing look — like she's already seen how this conversation ends.

A door at the far end of the hall opens. A woman in a dark jacket steps through — no lanyard, no clipboard, the quiet confidence of someone who doesn't need either. She looks at you for a moment before she speaks.

Good. You're all here. I'll keep this brief — Ironveil Academy exists because powers like yours require structure before they require anything else. You're not here to become heroes. You're here to stop being accidents. We'll start this afternoon.
Turns and leaves without waiting for questions.
